startup.name: Waffle
startup.description: AI video editor with hundreds of templates for reels, shorts and TikToks. Users make short form content for marketing or personal use. Two person team in London, Spring 2025 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: Start from the third party prior of about 1 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md). Two founders with an AI consumer app and no stated traction or retention, in a space dominated by large platform tools, give no lift. Consumer products without repeat usage are marked down in the factor table, so about 1 percent.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because template based short form video editing competes with free CapCut, Instagram Edits and well funded AI editors, and a two person team shows no retention or distribution edge. Consumer apps with no repeat usage rank low in the factor table.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --industry Consumer gave seed lower/known/upper 58%/72%/78%, cond 72% (n=79), ever. Months to seed median 11, p75 27 (n=57); AI tag anchor 64%.
anchors.adjustment_reason: About half the 0.72 consumer ever anchor, at the 2 times limit and justified by two named analogs with the same problem (ozone shut down, unfaze ai inactive), takeover risk 5 and a 19 month window.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M from angels and a small fund, the most common path for a 2 or 3 person team without revenue. Window is 19 months from 2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17; the YC deal alone does not count.
Institutional seed of $3M to $6M, the middle of the 2022 and later table (median about $3.5M to $4M).
Larger institutional seed of $6M to $12M, which the 2026 winners test showed is more common than forecasts assumed.
Hot round above $12M, possible only if the product shows fast usage; upside band.

ladder.why_it_fails: Investors will likely pass because free CapCut and Meta Edits cover the use case and the team has no retention data. Ozone shut down and unfaze ai went inactive, and consumer seed rounds need growth that a template editor without a distribution edge rarely shows. A seed would need clear paid conversion.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --industry Consumer gave series_a 23%/29%/43%, cond 40% (n=57).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Given a seed, a Series A inside 19 months is early (calibration p25 20 months for consumer), and retention risk is high, so well under half the ever anchor, about 0.18 times, justified by consumer analogs mojo and ozone that did not raise large rounds quickly.

bands.rationale: Thin Series A or extended seed below the 2022 and later p25 of $11M, typical when growth is slower than hoped.
Typical Series A near the 2022 and later median of about $14M to $15M.
Strong Series A of $16M to $30M when revenue growth is clear and a lead investor competes, above the 2022 and later p75 of about $20M.
Breakout Series A above $30M, possible only for a category leader with fast revenue growth; upside band.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A needs recurring revenue and healthy retention from a consumer product. Short form editing apps have high churn and heavy paid acquisition costs, and mojo and ozone did not reach large rounds. Waffle will likely miss because paid conversion stays small against free tools.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --industry Consumer gave series_b 9%/11%/29%, cond 39% (n=23). Ever.
anchors.adjustment_reason: About half the 0.39 anchor for competition from free platform tools; named analog mojo ended in acquisition.

bands.rationale: Down or flat round, below the 2022 and later p25 of $27M.
Typical Series B near the $32M to $40M median.
Upside band at the p75 of $55M and above.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B requires tens of millions in revenue. Consumer editing apps have been dominated by CapCut and platform owners, and past YC video tools were acquired for small amounts, so Waffle would likely be acquired before this stage if it works at all, and a failing path would end in a shutdown after the seed money runs out.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --industry Consumer gave series_c 2%/3%/21%, cond 22% (n=9). Ever.

bands.rationale: Smaller growth round or bridge financing below the 2022 and later series C p25 of about $50M.
Typical Series C near the $60M to $74M median.
Upside band for a category leader, above the 2022 and later series C p75 of about $100M.

ladder.why_it_fails: Growth rounds need category leadership in consumer video. With CapCut and Meta owning distribution, a template editor would need a huge paying base; consumer analogs rarely reach this stage and most end in small acquisitions instead, and the likely outcome for Waffle is a stall at the seed stage.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The usual end is a stall: consumer editing apps struggle with retention and platform owners give away editing for free. Ozone and unfaze ai are YC analogs that shut down or went inactive, and mojo ended in an acquisition after a long road. A template editor with no proprietary distribution is unlikely to exceed a small acquisition.

killers.risk: CapCut, Instagram Edits and Meta tools offer AI templates for free to hundreds of millions of users
killers.evidence: CapCut reportedly has hundreds of millions of users and Meta launched Edits in 2025.
killers.mitigation: Focus on a paying niche such as marketing teams and small businesses with brand templates.

killers.risk: Weak retention and acquisition cost for consumer apps
killers.evidence: Consumer cohorts show 35 percent inactive in the base rate set and unfaze ai went inactive.
killers.mitigation: Charge a subscription from day one and measure week 4 retention.

killers.risk: Template products are easy to copy
killers.evidence: Templates carry no technical moat and rivals such as opus clip and captions compete directly.
killers.mitigation: Build proprietary template generation from trend data.

competition_now.name: CapCut
competition_now.what: Free editor from ByteDance with AI features
competition_now.traction: Estimated hundreds of millions of monthly users

competition_now.name: Opus Clip and Descript
competition_now.traction: Early share in specific pain points

technical_complexity.rationale: A template based editor on top of existing video and generative models is buildable by two engineers in three months. Rendering speed and template quality are the work, and nothing needs a research breakthrough.

takeover_risk.rationale: Platform owners already ship AI templates and have distribution. The idea depends on social platforms that can restrict or copy features within a quarter.

evidence.claim: Short form video creation tools have large usage; CapCut is estimated at hundreds of millions of users
Consumers use free tools, so paid willingness is unproven

roadmap.goal: Evidence of retention in a niche
actions: Pick one creator or small business segment

pros.point: Huge usage of short form video makes a large pool of potential users
pros.evidence: CapCut estimates and short form growth show wide demand.

pros.point: Low build cost for a two person team
pros.evidence: Template editors layer on existing models and rendering libraries.

brand.name: Waffle
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Waffle" --era 2022+ : invented_or_proper, 6 chars, 2 syllables, no descriptor words.
brand.rationale: A playful short name that suits a consumer app and is easy to remember, much like past consumer YC names such as Instacart or Dropbox. It helps modestly with word of mouth but does not offset free incumbent tools.

narrative.headline: A consumer app in a space dominated by free platform tools; seed is possible but below the cohort anchor.
narrative.general_summary: Waffle is a template based AI video editor for short form content. Video creation demand is large, but CapCut and Meta give AI editing away free, funded AI editors and clippers compete, and consumer apps are marked down in the YC factor table for retention risk. A two person London team with no stated traction would need a paying niche to raise a seed above $1M inside 19 months. The probability is set below the consumer cohort anchor because of takeover risk and named analogs that failed. The odds do not rank Waffle against other companies, and later rounds are unlikely.

assumptions: Information limited to the input file and searches dated before 2025-04-07.
Seed means above about $1M from outside investors, excluding the YC deal.
No retention or revenue data assumed.
